lead: MPEG is a family of standards from the Moving Picture Experts Group. MPEG-1 and MPEG-2 made compressed video fit on CDs and DVDs. MPEG-4 adds object-based coding and the H.264/AVC codec used in phones and streaming. MPEG-7 is different: it does not compress media. It standardizes descriptions of multimedia content, so software can search, filter and manage audio, video and images. This chapter gives an overview of the family and the role of descriptors and description schemes in MPEG-7.
prereq: You need: Chapter 4.7 for motion compensation and perceptual audio coding, and Chapter 4.5 for the difference between a codec and a container.

sections.h3: MPEG-1 and MPEG-2: discs and broadcast

blocks.text: MPEG standards define a compressed bitstream and the decoder rules. A compliant encoder produces bits that a compliant decoder can read. The standard does not fix one encoder chip or one file extension.

MPEG-1 targeted about 1.5 Mbps video plus audio for Video CD. Its audio part has three layers; Layer III is the MP3 format used for music. MPEG-1 video uses motion-compensated prediction and a discrete cosine transform on 8×8 blocks.

MPEG-2 extends this to higher bit rates, interlaced television and transport streams. DVD-Video uses MPEG-2 video and MPEG-1 or MPEG-2 audio; digital television also uses MPEG-2. A size estimate uses the bit rate:

blocks.where: R is the bit rate in bits per second; t is the duration in seconds. Divide by 8 for bytes, then by 10⁹ for GB.

blocks.text: MPEG-4 is a family, not a single codec. It models a scene as audio-visual objects: a speaker, a background, a logo. Each object can be coded separately and composed at the decoder. This object-based idea supports interactive scenes and synthetic content. Many real files use MPEG-4 only as a simple video codec.

Part 10 of MPEG-4 is H.264/AVC, a widely used video codec. AVC adds better motion prediction, smaller transform blocks and in-loop filtering. It gives good quality at lower bit rates, so it appears in phones, video calls, streaming and broadcast. MPEG-4 audio includes AAC, used in phones and streaming.

The .mp4 file is a container from MPEG-4 Part 14; it can hold AVC video, AAC audio and metadata. The container is not the standard itself. An .mp4 extension alone does not prove the video codec; you must inspect the stream.

MPEG-7 does not compress audio or video. It standardizes descriptions of content. Some syllabi call it the Multimedia Content Description Interface. A description can say that a photo has a red shirt in the centre, that an audio clip is speech, or that a video shows a cricket ball moving left to right.

The basic unit is a descriptor (D). A descriptor represents a feature, such as colour, texture, shape, motion or audio timbre. A description scheme (DS) combines descriptors and states relationships: a shot contains a moving object; an image has regions; a segment has a title.

MPEG-7 uses a Description Definition Language, based on XML, to define descriptors and description schemes. Descriptions support search, filtering, browsing and rights metadata. They are not the media samples themselves. A search engine compares a query descriptor with stored descriptors, then ranks results.

MPEG-1, MPEG-2 and MPEG-4 are compression families. MPEG-7 is a description standard. MPEG-21 is a framework for delivery and rights; this chapter only notes it. Keep the names separate: MP3 is MPEG-1 Audio Layer III; MP4 is a container; MPEG-4 is a standard family.

Use MPEG-1 for old Video CD material, MPEG-2 for DVD and broadcast, MPEG-4/AVC for modern delivery, and MPEG-7 descriptions when you need to search or manage media. A player needs the right decoder for each stream, even when the container is supported.

In an exam, a question may give bit rate and time. Keep bits, bytes and GB separate. The worked example below uses 6 Mbps video and 448 kbps audio for one hour. Note that 6 Mbps = 6,000,000 bits/s, not 6,000,000 bytes/s. A 4.7 GB single-layer DVD has 4.7×10⁹ B, so the example fits with room for menus and error correction.

examples.question: A one-hour DVD video uses MPEG-2 video at 6 Mbps and audio at 448 kbps. Find the total size in bytes and in GB. Use 1 GB = 10⁹ B and 1 h = 3600 s.
steps: Video bit rate: R_v = 6 Mbps = 6,000,000 bits/s.
Audio bit rate: R_a = 448 kbps = 448,000 bits/s.
Total size = 2,901,600,000 ÷ 10⁹ = 2.9016 GB. This is below 4.7 GB.
examples.answer: The one-hour stream needs 2,901,600,000 B, or 2.9016 GB, so it fits a 4.7 GB single-layer DVD.
examples.check:
video_rate = 6_000_000
audio_rate = 448_000
t = 3600
video_bytes = (video_rate * t) // 8
audio_bytes = (audio_rate * t) // 8
total_bytes = video_bytes + audio_bytes
total_gb = total_bytes / 1_000_000_000
print(total_bytes)
print(total_gb)

traps: MPEG-7 is not a compression codec. A file described by MPEG-7 still needs a codec such as MPEG-2 or AVC for its media.
MP4 is a container, not the MPEG-4 compression standard. An .mp4 file can carry AVC video and AAC audio.
MP3 is MPEG-1 Audio Layer III. It is audio, not MPEG-2 video, and not a video codec.
Bit rate is in bits per second. Divide by 8 before you compare a size with a storage capacity in bytes or GB.
An .mpg or .mpeg extension does not identify the codec. It may hold MPEG-1 or MPEG-2 video.

quiz.q: What does MPEG stand for, and what does the MPEG-7 standard describe?
quiz.a: MPEG stands for Moving Picture Experts Group. MPEG-7 is the Multimedia Content Description Interface; it standardizes descriptions of multimedia content, not compression.

quiz.q: Why can MPEG-7 not replace MPEG-4 for playing a video?
quiz.a: MPEG-4 contains video codecs such as AVC that compress and decode pixels. MPEG-7 only describes features and relationships; it carries no decoded media and cannot reconstruct frames.

quiz.q: A 2-hour video uses 4 Mbps. Find the video size in bytes and GB. Use 1 GB = 10⁹ B.
A file is named clip.mp4. Can you conclude it uses MPEG-4 Part 2 video? Explain.
quiz.a: No. .mp4 is a container from MPEG-4 Part 14. It may carry AVC/H.264, HEVC, AAC audio or other streams; inspect the codec identifiers.

quiz.q: Define descriptor and description scheme in MPEG-7.
quiz.a: A descriptor represents one feature such as colour or motion. A description scheme combines descriptors and their relationships.

quiz.q: Give one search task that an MPEG-7 colour descriptor supports.
quiz.a: Find images whose central region has a colour similar to a query colour. The engine compares colour descriptors and ranks matches; it does not compare raw pixels only.

quiz.q: Why are descriptions useful when media files are large and stored on many servers?
quiz.a: Descriptions are small metadata. A search engine can filter by descriptors before fetching large media, saving bandwidth and time. It can also rank, browse and manage rights without decoding every file.

beyond: Not for the exam. MPEG-7 concepts appear in media asset management, photo libraries and video search, where metadata is stored beside the media. Modern streaming uses codecs such as H.264/AVC and HEVC, with segmented delivery; descriptions can sit in the catalogue layer. Search next for MPEG-7 visual descriptors, description schemes, MPEG-21 and MPEG-DASH. Machine-learning features now compete with hand-designed descriptors for search.
